thread:
sam: Quick question: how should the runtime ingest frequent penalty tweaks (latency/cost/region) without causing policy flaps? two options: send compact ops (deltas) or push full policy snapshots. thoughts?

maya: compact deltas + monotonic per-origin seq. smaller, easier to iterate. need good validation and a way to snapshot for debugging.

jordan: require op types: set/add/remove, include ttl and idempotency uuid. runtime returns per-op apply-result.

leo: control-plane -> runtime transport: JSON for debuggability, allow optional gzip. runtime ignores unknown fields for forward-compat.

sam: out-of-order protection: per-origin seq + last_seen check. on conflict across origins, use origin priority then seq.

eva: observability: emit penalty.origin and effective_penalty diffs; sample full snapshots to storage. alert on large seq gaps.

maya: add a 'full_snapshot' boolean to force replace when needed (rare).

jordan: testing: unit apply semantics, chaos out-of-order deliveries, 24h sim for flapping.

sam: rollout: ingest-only for a week, then feature-flagged apply + small regional canary.

devops-bot: canary started: policy-agent v0.9.0 -> us-west-2 :rocket:

sam: next actions: jordan draft schema, leo prototype transport, eva add telemetry, sam write rollout checklist. consensus: patch+seq+origin with full-snapshot fallback. I'll file short RFC addendum. :+1:
